## Overview

`Button` is the MakeMyTrip Cosmos action control: a single horizontal auto-layout row that hugs its label, with an optional leading icon, an optional trailing icon, and a loading spinner, all drawn as flat siblings of the `Label` text. Its API is nine properties — `hierarchy`, `intent`, and `size` from the Figma variant axes, `label` from the text property, the `leadingIcon` / `trailingIcon` slot enums with their shared `icon` glyph, and the two persistent state booleans `isLoading` and `isDisabled`; the Figma `State` axis is decomposed rather than exposed, so hover, press, and focus belong to the platform. Geometry varies only with `size` (every box metric resolves to a `button/*` component variable), while 85 colour tokens are indexed by `hierarchy × intent` and re-pointed per state — and the focus indicator is a dedicated `Focus Ring` rectangle drawn outside the button box, not a border change. For screen readers the component is exactly one focus stop on all three platforms: the label merges into the accessible name and every icon and the spinner are hidden, with `aria-disabled="true"` recommended over the native `disabled` attribute whenever a disabled button must stay discoverable.

**Variant axes.** 4 axes across 120 variants — **Hierarchy** (Primary, Secondary, Tertiary, Text; default `Primary`) · **State** (Default, Hover, Pressed, Focus, Disabled; default `Default`) · **Size** (Medium, Large, Small; default `Medium`) · **Intent** (Default, Destructive; default `Default`). Only **Size** changes geometry; **Hierarchy** and **Intent** are paint-only; **State** is not a consumer-set property (it maps to CSS pseudo-classes and `isDisabled`).

## API

_Confidence: high._

> State is not a consumer-set property. The Figma `State` axis (Default, Hover, Pressed, Focus, Disabled) is decomposed: hovered, pressed, and focused are transient and belong to the platform (`:hover`, `:active`, `:focus-visible`), while the one persistent state becomes `isDisabled`. See the state mapping for the Figma-option-to-runtime-condition table.
>
> Content-row precedence: the button lays its content out in a single horizontal row in the order `isLoading` spinner -> `leadingIcon` -> `label` -> `trailingIcon`. The design model does NOT suppress one when another is set — the extracted geometry proves all four render simultaneously (medium/primary measures 147px wide with the spinner, both icons, and the label all visible, against 75px for label-only). Engineers must therefore decide the loading treatment themselves; the recommended contract is that `isLoading=true` replaces `leadingIcon` and `trailingIcon` with the spinner and keeps `label` visible, and that `isDisabled=true` makes the button non-interactive regardless of `isLoading`.
>
> Disabled implementation tradeoff: the native `disabled` attribute removes the button from the tab order, which makes any tooltip or explanation of *why* it is disabled unreachable by keyboard and screen-reader users. `aria-disabled="true"` keeps the button focusable and announceable while you suppress the activation handler yourself. Prefer `aria-disabled="true"` whenever the disabled button must stay discoverable, and reserve the native attribute for cases where the button carries no explanatory affordance.
>
> Focus presentation: the Focus state is drawn as a dedicated `Focus Ring` rectangle behind the button rather than a border change, so it maps to the design system's focus-ring / focus-ring-offset / focus-ring-width tokens and must be reproduced with an outline plus offset (not by mutating the button's own border). Render it on `:focus-visible` only.
>
> One shared icon glyph: Figma exposes a single `Icon` instance-swap property for both icon slots, so the leading and trailing slots cannot be given different glyphs from this component's API as extracted. Treat `icon` as the shared glyph until the design exposes a per-slot swap.

| Property | Type | Values | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| hierarchy | enum | primary \| secondary \| tertiary \| text | primary | Visual priority of the action. Figma names this axis 'Hierarchy'; the name is kept because it means visual priority, not style family. Use primary for the single main action per view, text for inline low-emphasis actions. |
| intent | enum | default \| destructive | default | Semantic meaning of the action. Orthogonal to hierarchy — destructive recolors any hierarchy rather than replacing it. Use destructive only for irreversible actions. |
| size | enum | small \| medium \| large | medium | Controls min-height, horizontal/vertical padding, gap, icon size, and label type ramp. See the Structure section for measured values per size. |
| label | string | (string) | – | Visible text and the accessible name. Figma ships the placeholder string "Button" as the TEXT property default; that is placeholder copy, not a usable default, so treat the property as required and always supply real action text. |
| leadingIcon | enum | none \| icon | none | Whether an icon renders before the label. Merged from the Figma `Icon Leading` visibility boolean — false maps to none. Decorative: must be aria-hidden and never a separate focus stop. |
| trailingIcon | enum | none \| icon | none | Whether an icon renders after the label. Merged from the Figma `Icon Trailing` visibility boolean — false maps to none. Decorative: must be aria-hidden and never a separate focus stop. |
| icon | instance | (instance) | chevron-right | Only meaningful when leadingIcon or trailingIcon = icon. Glyph rendered in whichever icon slot is enabled. Figma exposes ONE instance-swap for both slots, so leading and trailing share this value as extracted; see generalNotes. |
| isLoading | boolean | true \| false | false | Renders the spinner and marks the button busy (`aria-busy="true"`). The spinner is decorative and aria-hidden; the busy state is announced on the button itself. Suppress activation while loading. |
| isDisabled | boolean | true \| false | false | The one persistent state extracted from the Figma `State` axis. Render: applies the disabled fill/label/border tokens for the current hierarchy and intent. ARIA: `aria-disabled="true"` (preferred) or the native `disabled` attribute — see the tradeoff in generalNotes. Focus announcement: with `aria-disabled` the button stays in the tab order and announces 'dimmed'/'disabled' after its name; with the native attribute it leaves the tab order entirely and is never announced. |

## Structure

### Anatomy

```text
Button (component set · 58:202)
├─ Focus Ring (rectangle · 57:3) · decorative
├─ Spinner (instance · 57:4) · referenced · a11y-hidden
│  └─ Ellipse (ellipse)
├─ Icon Leading (instance · 57:5) · referenced · a11y-hidden
│  └─ Vector (vector)
├─ Label (text) · decorative
└─ Icon Trailing (instance · 57:7) · a11y-hidden
   └─ Vector (vector)
```

_Confidence: medium — 1 inferred row(s); 0 non-default-size row(s) unmeasured._

> Every box metric on the Button comes from the `button/*` component variable collection, which has a single mode — there is no density or theme axis, so dimensions change with Size only. Hierarchy, Intent and State never change geometry: Hierarchy and Intent are paint-only, and State adds exactly one structural element (the focus ring).
>
> State is not a consumer-set property. Model it with CSS pseudo-classes plus the disabled condition (`enabled, not interacting` / `:hover` / `:active` / `:focus-visible` / `isDisabled === true`), which is why the interaction-state section uses runtime conditions as column headers.
>
> Focus ring: a dedicated `Focus Ring` rectangle, not a border on the button. It maps to `button/focus-ring` (color/border-brand), `button/focus-ring-offset` → space/3xs (2) and `button/focus-ring-width` → border-width-2 (2), and it renders 4 outside the button box on every side. `clipsContent` must stay false and the ring must stay out of the auto-layout flow.
>
> Accessibility: the button is a single focus stop. The leading icon, trailing icon and loading spinner are presentational and must be aria-hidden — never separate focus stops. For the Disabled state, the native `disabled` attribute removes the element from the tab order, which makes tooltips and explanations unreachable; `aria-disabled="true"` keeps it focusable and announceable. Prefer `aria-disabled` whenever the disabled button must stay discoverable.
>
> Anomalies to fix in Figma: (1) `button/gap-lg` and `button/gap-md` both alias space/xs, so the icon–label gap does not grow from Medium (8) to Large (8); (2) `button/icon-size-lg` and `button/icon-size-md` both alias icon/sm, so the glyph stays 20 at Large; (3) the default variant (Hierarchy=Primary, State=Default, Size=Medium, Intent=Default) is the only one of 40 Medium variants bound to `button/gap-sm` (4) while the other 39 use `button/gap-md` (8) — a per-variant binding slip, not a state behaviour; (4) root `cornerRadius` (8) and root `strokeWeight` (1) are literals even though `button/radius` (radius/md → 8) and `button/border-width` (border-width-1) exist; (5) the focus ring’s 12 radius and 2 stroke are literals rather than bound to the focus-ring tokens.
>
> Border presence is expressed through stroke opacity, not stroke weight: all four hierarchies keep `strokeWeight: 1`, and only Secondary paints it (opacity 1). Implement Primary, Tertiary and Text as borderless — or as a transparent 1 border — so the box metrics stay identical across hierarchies.
>
> Coverage: the component contains no FRAME nodes at all. The variant root is a COMPONENT and its five children are a RECTANGLE, three INSTANCEs and a TEXT node, so the per-FRAME coverage matrix walked 0 frames (`framesWalked: 0`, `complete: true`). The root’s own auto-layout properties — padding, itemSpacing, cornerRadius, borderWidth and borderAlign — are all documented in the Button sizes section, and the three INSTANCE children are referenced components whose internals belong to the Icon specs.
>
> Evidence limits: `variants[*].revealedTree` carries only a root node (Phase G captured no children) and no `revealedByVariantName` block exists, and this run had no Figma link, so no delta measurement was possible. No row was left unmeasured as a result: the baseline `treeHierarchical` walks hidden children with full dimensions, and `crossVariant.axisDiffs` supplies the all-booleans-enabled geometry that confirms the icon and spinner measurements.
>
> Extraction warning carried over from the plugin: 124 raw-hex colorWalk entries inside crossed INSTANCE boundaries were dropped (Icon / spinner 123, Icon / chevron-right 1). Tokened entries were preserved. This affects colour evidence only — no structural measurement depends on it.

### Button sizes

Root container geometry across the size axis. The button is a single horizontal auto-layout row with flat children (focus ring, spinner, leading icon, label, trailing icon) — there are no wrapper frames. Every box metric is bound to the `button/*` component token collection and only Size changes it: Hierarchy, Intent and State leave the geometry untouched.

| Spec | Large | Medium | Small | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Container | – | – | – | Variant root — one horizontal row holding spinner, leading icon, label and trailing icon. |
| ├ minHeight | button/min-height-lg (48) | button/min-height-md (40) | button/min-height-sm (32) | Height floor per size (space/6xl → 48, 5xl → 40, 3xl → 32). Only Large clears the 44 WCAG 2.5.8 target — give Medium and Small extra hit area when they stand alone. |
| ├ heightMode | fill | fill | fill | Root fills its parent vertically, so minHeight is the real height floor rather than a fixed height. |
| ├ widthMode | hug | hug | hug | Width hugs the label — never hard-code a width, the same button must absorb longer translations. |
| ├ verticalPadding | button/padding-y-lg (12) | button/padding-y-md (8) | button/padding-y-sm (4) | Vertical inset halves at each step down (12 → 8 → 4) so the label keeps its optical centre as minHeight shrinks. |
| ├ horizontalPadding | button/padding-x-lg (20) | button/padding-x-md (16) | button/padding-x-sm (12) | Side inset steps space/lg → md → sm (20 → 16 → 12), always wider than the vertical inset so the label never looks cramped. |
| ├ itemSpacing | button/gap-lg (8) | button/gap-md (8) | button/gap-sm (4) | Gap between spinner/icon and label. `button/gap-lg` and `button/gap-md` both alias space/xs, so the gap does not grow from Medium to Large; only Small steps down to 4. |
| ├ cornerRadius | 8 | 8 | 8 | Fixed 8 at every size — a rounded rectangle, not a pill. Written as a literal even though `button/radius` (radius/md → 8) exists; bind it to keep shape themable. |
| ├ borderWidth | 1 | 1 | 1 | Every hierarchy carries a 1 stroke, but only Secondary paints it (the others hold stroke opacity at 0), so all four hierarchies share identical box metrics. `button/border-width` (border-width-1) exists but is unbound. |
| ├ borderAlign | inside | inside | inside | Inside alignment keeps the stroke within minHeight, so adding a border never changes the button footprint. |
| ├ horizontalAlignment | center | center | center | Children centre along the main axis, so the row grows symmetrically as icons are added. |
| ├ verticalAlignment | center | center | center | Icons and label share one optical centre line regardless of glyph height. |
| └ clipsContent | false | false | false | Must stay off: the focus ring is drawn beyond the button box and would otherwise be clipped. |
| Label | – | – | – | Text child — the only visible child in the default configuration. |
| ├ textStyle | label/large/bold | label/medium/bold | label/small/bold | One bound text style per size; no inline type overrides anywhere in the 120-variant set. |
| ├ widthMode | hug | hug | hug | Label hugs its own text — truncation is the consumer’s decision, not the component’s. |
| └ heightMode | hug | hug | hug | Height follows the bound style at each size, which is what drives the 40 / 48 / 32 box with padding. |

### Focus ring

The focus indicator is a dedicated `Focus Ring` rectangle rather than an outline on the button itself. It sits outside the button box and is revealed only in the Focus state, so it needs the design system’s focus-ring, focus-ring-offset and focus-ring-width tokens to be implemented as an outline plus offset — not as a border on the button.

| Spec | Large | Medium | Small | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Focus Ring | – | – | – | Rectangle drawn 4 outside the button box on every side (2 offset + 2 ring width); hidden in every state except :focus-visible. |
| ├ height | 56 | 48 | 40 | minHeight plus 4 on each side. The ring’s width tracks the button’s hug width the same way, so implement it as an outline offset rather than a fixed box. |
| ├ borderWidth | 2 | 2 | 2 | Ring thickness, constant across sizes; matches `button/focus-ring-width` → border-width-2 (2). Stroke colour comes from `button/focus-ring` (color/border-brand). |
| ├ borderAlign | inside | inside | inside | Inside alignment on the ring rectangle, so the 2 stroke sits within the measured ring box instead of growing it further. |
| [inferred via button/focus-ring-offset] ├ focusRingOffset | 2 | 2 | 2 | Clear gap between the button edge and the ring stroke, resolved from `button/focus-ring-offset` → space/3xs → spacing/2 (2). Offset 2 + ring width 2 accounts for the 4-per-side ring box. |
| ├ cornerRadius | 12 | 12 | 12 | Root radius 8 plus the 4 ring expansion keeps the corners concentric; equals radius/lg (12), though it is a literal in Figma. |
| └ widthMode | fixed | fixed | fixed | Fixed rectangle sized off the button box — keep it out of the auto-layout flow so revealing focus never adds width. |

| Container | – | – | – | – | – | Same root geometry in every state — no reflow when the pointer or focus enters. |
| ├ minHeight | button/min-height-md (40) | button/min-height-md (40) | button/min-height-md (40) | button/min-height-md (40) | button/min-height-md (40) | Identical in all five states, so hover and press must not shift surrounding layout. |
| ├ itemSpacing | button/gap-sm (4) | button/gap-md (8) | button/gap-md (8) | button/gap-md (8) | button/gap-md (8) | Not a state behaviour: the Default / Medium variant is the only one of the 40 Medium variants bound to `button/gap-sm`. Treat `button/gap-md` (8) as the intended Medium gap and fix the binding on that variant. |
| ├ borderWidth | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | Stroke weight is state-independent; states change only the stroke’s colour and opacity, so no reflow on hover or press. |
| ├ focusRingVisibility | hidden | hidden | hidden | visible | hidden | The Focus Ring rectangle is the only structural difference between states — reveal it on :focus-visible, never on :hover or :active. |
| └ cornerRadius | 8 | 8 | 8 | 8 | 8 | Radius holds across states; press feedback is colour-only, with no shape change. |

## Color

_Confidence: high._ _Reconciliation: 3 auto-fixed, 1 retried, 0 unresolved._

> Color is driven by Hierarchy x Intent for surface, border and label tokens; the State axis only re-points those same token families (default/hover/pressed/disabled). Token names are verbatim Figma resolutions: container, border, label and focus-ring tokens carry WEB codeSyntax (CSS custom properties); icon glyph fills resolve to variable path names (color/icon-*). Size is color-irrelevant — all 120 variants carry identical tokens across Small, Medium and Large, so sections use the Medium representative. No light/dark or density color modes exist: the primitives, semantic and component variable collections each expose exactly one mode. Cells whose hex is null carry a bound token painted at zero alpha (Primary/Tertiary/Text borders, Secondary/Text surfaces at rest) — the token is real, the paint is invisible. Focus is drawn by a dedicated Focus Ring rectangle (var(--button-focus-ring)) that is hidden in every other state, hence "none" outside the Focus column; its offset and width live in the structure spec. Leading and trailing icons are Icon / chevron-right instances whose fills the button owns; they are hidden until leadingIcon/trailingIcon is set to icon, so their tokens apply only in those configurations. Loading spinner (Icon / spinner, gated by the Loading boolean / isLoading prop) is represented as a row in every section, but its cells are unmeasurable (—): the Icon / spinner instance paints its Ellipse arc with raw hex, and the extraction dropped all 123 of those raw-hex entries at the crossed INSTANCE boundary, so neither a token nor a hex survives in _base.json. No spinner token was invented; the canonical spinner color spec lives in the Icon / spinner component's own spec. One measured inconsistency: Primary / Default trailing icon at Medium size resolves to color/icon-brand in the Default state while Large and Small resolve to color/icon-inverse — likely an unintended override. No composite paint styles and no shadow or effect entries exist anywhere in the walk; every element is a single solid paint.

## Voice / Screen reader

_Confidence: high._

> - Single focus stop. The button is one focus stop on every platform; the visible Label merges into it as the accessible name. The leading icon, trailing icon, and loading spinner are presentational and must never be separate focus stops.
> - Merge mechanisms differ by platform but the result is identical: iOS uses `.accessibilityElement(children: .combine)`, Android uses `semantics(mergeDescendants = true)`, and the web gets it for free because a native `<button>` exposes its text content as the accessible name.
> - Decorative children must be hidden: `Icon Leading` and `Icon Trailing` (`Icon / chevron-right`) and `Spinner` (`Icon / spinner`) take `.accessibilityHidden(true)` / `contentDescription = null` / `aria-hidden="true"`.
> - Interaction states are platform-owned, not consumer-set props. `:hover`, `:active`, and `:focus-visible` change only the rendered appearance and must not change the accessible name, role, or announcement. Do not model them as an API enum.
> - Focus indication: the `Focus Ring` rectangle layer is a purely visual affordance drawn on `:focus-visible` using the design system's focus-ring / focus-ring-offset / focus-ring-width tokens. Never expose it to assistive technology and never suppress it — it is the visible half of the same requirement the screen reader satisfies audibly.
> - Loading: `isLoading` (Figma `Loading#58:3`) shows the spinner and must be announced as busy state on the button itself (`accessibilityValue` / `stateDescription` / `aria-busy="true"`), never by moving focus to the spinner. Keep the accessible name stable while loading so the stop does not appear to change identity. Block activation while loading.
> - Disabled: prefer `aria-disabled="true"` (iOS `.notEnabled` trait, Android `disabled()`) over the native `disabled` attribute when the button must stay discoverable. The native attribute removes the button from the tab order entirely, which makes any tooltip or explanation of *why* it is unavailable unreachable by keyboard and screen reader. When you use `aria-disabled`, you must also block the click and keydown handlers yourself — it changes semantics, not behavior.
> - Accessible name quality: the label must describe the action, not the appearance ("Book now", not "Blue button"). Do not include the word "button" in the label; every platform appends the role itself.
> - Focus order stability: do not reorder focus across states; keep the stop index stable so user gestures remain predictable.
> - Announcement length: do not stuff the accessible name with the hint, value, and busy/disabled state; each belongs on its dedicated property.
> - Platform parity: do not document a merge on one platform and a breakout on another without an explicit note. Here all three platforms merge identically to a single stop, so no divergence note is required.

### State: enabled, not interacting / :hover / :active / :focus-visible

Grouped entry. The Figma `State` axis values Default, Hover, Pressed, and Focus are visually distinct but semantically identical to a screen reader: same single focus stop, same role, same accessible name, same announcement. Hover and pressed are pointer-only affordances; `:focus-visible` only draws the `Focus Ring` rectangle and does not change what is announced. Documented against the Default variant as the representative member.

#### VoiceOver (iOS)

| Property | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Announcement | "Button, button" |  |
| accessibilityLabel | "Button" | Taken from the visible `Label` TEXT layer (Figma text property `Label#58:0`); the label merges into this stop rather than being its own element. |
| accessibilityValue | – | A plain action button carries no value in the resting or interacting states. |
| accessibilityTraits | .isButton | Role for the single focus stop; matches the design system's `button` role. |
| accessibilityHint | – | Add a hint only when the outcome is non-obvious, e.g. "Opens payment options"; never restate the label. |
| accessibilityElement | .accessibilityElement(children: .combine) | Merges `Label` and any icon child into one element so VoiceOver lands on the button exactly once. |
| Icon Leading / Icon Trailing | .accessibilityHidden(true) | `Icon / chevron-right` instances are presentational chevrons and carry no meaning beyond the label. |
| Do NOT | Do not read the label twice | The `Label` layer merges into this stop's name; it must not also be exposed as a separate accessibility element. |
| Do NOT | Do not announce the decorative icons | Mark `Icon Leading` and `Icon Trailing` `.accessibilityHidden(true)` — announcing "chevron right" adds noise and no information. |

#### TalkBack (Android)

| Property | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Announcement | "Button, button, double-tap to activate" |  |
| contentDescription | "Button" | From the visible `Label` layer; omit the word "button" because TalkBack appends the role itself. |
| role | Role.Button | Declares the tappable action so TalkBack offers the "double-tap to activate" hint. |
| stateDescription | – | No state to convey while enabled; hover and pressed are not TalkBack-visible states. |
| semantics(mergeDescendants = true) | true | Collapses `Label` and the icon children into a single traversal stop. |
| Icon Leading / Icon Trailing | contentDescription = null | Presentational chevrons; `null` (not an empty string) keeps them out of the traversal order. |
| Do NOT | Do not read the label twice | With `mergeDescendants = true` the `Label` composable must not also set its own `semantics { }` block. |
| Do NOT | Do not announce the decorative icons | Use `contentDescription = null` or `invisibleToUser()` on the chevron icons. |

#### ARIA (Web)

| Property | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Announcement | "Button, button" |  |
| element | <button type="button"> | Prefer the native element over `role="button"` — it brings focusability, Enter/Space activation, and the `button` role for free. |
| role | button (implicit) | Matches the design system's declared ARIA role; do not add `role="button"` redundantly to a native `<button>`. |
| accessible name | "Button" (text content) | The visible `Label` text is the accessible name; add `aria-label` only for an icon-only configuration with no visible text. |
| tabindex | – | A native `<button>` is already in the tab order; never add `tabindex` to make it focusable. |
| svg icons | aria-hidden="true" focusable="false" | Applies to the leading and trailing chevrons so they neither announce nor become focus stops in IE-era SVG behavior. |
| :focus-visible | Focus Ring (focus-ring / focus-ring-offset / focus-ring-width) | Visual-only affordance drawn by the `Focus Ring` layer; it has no ARIA representation and must never be removed without a replacement. |
| Do NOT | Do not read the label twice | Do not set `aria-label` alongside visible text — `aria-label` overrides the text content and breaks voice-control "click Button". |
| Do NOT | Do not announce the decorative icons | Mark the chevron SVGs `aria-hidden="true"`; they are never separate focus stops. |

### State: isLoading === true

Loading is the top-level boolean `isLoading` (Figma `Loading#58:3`, layer `Spinner`), not a `State` axis value — set the boolean on the preview instance in addition to the variant props below. The focus stop count is unchanged (1): the spinner replaces the label's leading space visually but must be announced as busy state on the button itself. Activation should be blocked while loading.

#### VoiceOver (iOS)

| Property | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Announcement | "Button, loading, button" |  |
| accessibilityLabel | "Button" | Keep the name stable while loading so the stop does not appear to change identity mid-interaction. |
| accessibilityValue | "Loading" | Busy state belongs on the value, which VoiceOver reads after the label and before the trait. |
| accessibilityTraits | [.isButton, .notEnabled] | Add `.notEnabled` only when activation is actually blocked during loading, so the trait matches real behaviour. |
| AccessibilityNotification.Announcement | "Loading" posted on transition | Announce the start of the async work; VoiceOver does not re-read a stop the user is already on. |
| Spinner | .accessibilityHidden(true) | `Icon / spinner` is a decorative indicator; the busy state is carried by the button's value, not by the glyph. |
| Do NOT | Do not announce the spinner as a standalone element | Fold the indicator into this stop's `accessibilityValue`; a focusable spinner strands the user on a nameless element. |

#### TalkBack (Android)

| Property | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Announcement | "Button, loading, button, double-tap to activate" |  |
| contentDescription | "Button" | Unchanged from the enabled state; the busy condition is state, not name. |
| stateDescription | "Loading" | TalkBack reads `stateDescription` after the role, which is exactly where a transient busy state belongs. |
| role | Role.Button | Role is unchanged — a loading button is still a button. |
| liveRegion | LiveRegionMode.Polite | Announces the transition into and out of loading without interrupting whatever TalkBack is currently reading. |
| Spinner | contentDescription = null | `Icon / spinner` is decorative; the merged parent already carries the loading state. |
| Do NOT | Do not announce the spinner as a standalone element | Fold the indicator into `stateDescription` rather than giving the spinner its own semantics block. |

#### ARIA (Web)

| Property | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Announcement | "Button, button, busy" |  |
| element | <button type="button" aria-busy="true"> | `aria-busy` is the canonical web signal that the control's work is in flight. |
| accessible name | "Button" (text content) | Keep the visible label mounted while loading; swapping it for a bare spinner destroys the accessible name. |
| aria-disabled | true (when activation is blocked) | Prevents repeat submissions while keeping the button focusable and its explanation reachable. |
| status region | <span role="status"> announcing "Loading" | Optional companion for long operations; reference it with `aria-describedby` rather than stuffing the name. |
| spinner svg | aria-hidden="true" | The `Spinner` layer is decorative; `aria-busy` already conveys the state. |
| Do NOT | Do not announce the spinner as a standalone element | Fold the indicator into `aria-busy` on the button; do not give the SVG `role="img"` with a "loading" label. |
| Do NOT | Do not list the status region as a focus stop | It is announced via `role="status"` / `aria-live="polite"`, never by moving focus into it. |

### State: isDisabled === true

Maps to the Figma `State=Disabled` variant, surfaced in the API as the top-level boolean `isDisabled`. Two implementations produce different focus behaviour: the native `disabled` attribute removes the button from the tab order entirely (focus stop count 0, and any tooltip explaining why it is unavailable becomes unreachable), while `aria-disabled="true"` keeps it focusable and announceable (focus stop count 1). Recommended: `aria-disabled="true"` whenever the button must stay discoverable — the tables below document that recommended configuration. If you use the native attribute instead, this state carries zero focus stops and the component is inert.

#### VoiceOver (iOS)

| Property | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Announcement | "Button, dimmed, button" |  |
| accessibilityLabel | "Button" | Unchanged from the enabled state; disabled is a trait, never part of the name. |
| accessibilityTraits | [.isButton, .notEnabled] | `.notEnabled` makes VoiceOver say "dimmed" while the element stays reachable by swipe. |
| isEnabled / .disabled(true) | false / true | SwiftUI's `.disabled(true)` keeps the element in the accessibility tree, which is the iOS equivalent of the recommended `aria-disabled` behaviour. |
| accessibilityHint | "Select a date to continue" (example) | Explain *why* the control is unavailable; this is the payoff for keeping the stop reachable. |
| Do NOT | Do not remove the button from the accessibility tree | `.accessibilityHidden(true)` on a disabled control hides the reason it is disabled; use `.notEnabled` instead. |

#### TalkBack (Android)

| Property | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Announcement | "Button, button, disabled" |  |
| contentDescription | "Button" | Unchanged; TalkBack appends "disabled" from semantics, so never bake it into the description. |
| role | Role.Button | Role survives the disabled state — the user still needs to know what kind of control it is. |
| semantics { disabled() } | applied | Marks the control unavailable while leaving it in the traversal order, matching the recommended web behaviour. |
| stateDescription | – | Leave empty — `disabled()` already produces the "disabled" announcement; setting it duplicates the word. |
| Do NOT | Do not use invisibleToUser() for disabled | Hiding the control removes the explanation of why the action is unavailable. |

#### ARIA (Web)

| Property | Value | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Announcement | "Button, button, unavailable" (NVDA) / "Button, dimmed, button" (VoiceOver) |  |
| element | <button type="button" aria-disabled="true"> | Recommended: keeps the button in the tab order so its name, role, and explanation stay reachable. |
| aria-disabled | true | Conveys unavailability to assistive technology without changing focusability. |
| disabled (native attribute) | Alternative — not recommended when discoverability matters | Removes the button from the tab order and from pointer/keyboard events, so an associated tooltip or explanation can never be reached by keyboard or screen reader; this state then has zero focus stops. |
| aria-describedby | id of the reason text | Pair with `aria-disabled` to explain the blocker, e.g. "Select a date to continue" — impossible with the native attribute. |
| event handlers | Blocked in click and keydown | `aria-disabled` changes semantics only; the component must reject activation itself. |
| Do NOT | Do not use the native disabled attribute when the button must stay discoverable | It removes the stop from the focus order; prefer `aria-disabled="true"` so the stop remains focusable and announceable. |
| Do NOT | Do not set aria-disabled="true" without blocking activation | A button that announces "unavailable" but still fires its handler is worse than no signal at all. |

## Validation against the Cosmos token pipeline

This spec was cross-checked against `tokens/tokens.json` and the compiled `dist/web/tokens.css` after generation. Cosmos already ships 100 `component.button` tokens, so this component has independent ground truth — unusual for a first uSpec run, and the reason Button was chosen for the pilot.

### Accuracy

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `var(--button-*)` references that resolve to a shipped CSS custom property | 81 / 81 |
| Hex values quoted alongside a token that match the compiled value | 86 / 86 |
| `button/*` Figma token names that exist under `component.button` | 21 / 21 |
| Numeric dimension claims that match the resolved token value | 15 / 15 |
| `color/*` semantic references that exist under `semantic` | 5 / 5 |
| `component.button` tokens documented somewhere in this spec | 100 / 100 |

No fabricated token names, no fabricated hex values, and no invented dimensions. Where a value was genuinely unmeasurable (the loading spinner fill, dropped at the `Icon / spinner` instance boundary) the spec renders em-dashes and points at the icon's own spec rather than guessing.

### Token defects this spec surfaced

Five Figma-side binding issues, each confirmed against the token source:

1. **`button/gap-lg` and `button/gap-md` both alias `space.xs`**, so the icon-label gap stays 8 from Medium to Large. Resolution chain: `button.gap-lg -> space.xs -> spacing.8`.
2. **`button/icon-size-lg` and `button/icon-size-md` both alias `icon.sm`**, so the glyph stays 20 at Large. Only Small steps down to `icon.xs` (16).
3. **`button/radius` exists but is unbound in Figma.** `component.button.radius -> radius.md` compiles to `--button-radius: 8px`, yet the component set hardcodes `cornerRadius: 8` as a literal.
4. **`button/border-width` exists but is unbound.** `component.button.border-width -> borderWidth.1` compiles to `--button-border-width: 1px`, while the root carries a literal `strokeWeight: 1`.
5. **Per-variant `gap` binding slip.** The default variant (Primary / Default / Medium / Default) is the only one of 40 Medium variants bound to `button/gap-sm` (4); the other 39 use `button/gap-md` (8).

### The focus-ring gap

Confirmed as predicted. Figma models focus as 24 distinct `State=Focus` variants, but the token layer exposes focus as three global values with no hierarchy or intent axis:

- `button.focus-ring -> color.border-brand -> color.brand.600` = `#086BC5`
- `button.focus-ring-offset -> space.3xs -> spacing.2` = `2px`
- `button.focus-ring-width -> borderWidth.2` = `2px`

The consequence is visible in the Color section: all eight hierarchy/intent combinations quote `var(--button-focus-ring)` at `#086BC5`, so **destructive buttons render a brand-blue focus ring**. That is a token modelling decision to confirm or fix, not an extraction error. The Focus Ring rectangle's own `cornerRadius: 12` and `strokeWeight: 2` are also literals rather than bound to the focus-ring tokens.

### Naming observation

Destructive icons resolve to `color/icon-warning` (`color.red.700`, `#C10007`). The semantic palette uses `warning` for red, so destructive and warning share one icon token. Worth deciding whether Cosmos wants a distinct `icon-destructive` or `icon-error` alias, since destructive and warning are different intents.

### Naming translation

Figma variable names arrive in Tokens Studio form, not Figma path form. Container, border, label, and focus-ring tokens carry WEB `codeSyntax`, so they emerge already as `var(--button-bg-primary-default)`. Icon glyph fills have no `codeSyntax` and emerge as variable paths (`color/icon-brand`). Any future automation needs to handle both shapes.

### One measured inconsistency

Primary / Default trailing icon resolves to `color/icon-brand` at Medium but `color/icon-inverse` at Large and Small. A brand-blue glyph on the brand-blue Primary surface would be nearly invisible, so Medium is likely the mistake.
